title: Global Homelessness
description: How homelessness is distributed across the world, scaled to a global village of 1,000 people.

sections.heading: Homelessness Distribution in a Global Village of 1,000 People
sections.caption: Here is the visual breakdown of how continental homelessness translates to a global village of 1,000 people, calculated using a world baseline of 8 billion people.

sources.title: United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat)
sources.description: Provides the foundational baseline estimates for global housing deficits, slum populations, and informal settlements across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

sources.title: European Federation of National Organisations Working with the Homeless (FEANTSA)
sources.description: Publishes the annual Overview of Housing Exclusion in Europe, which tracks shelter usage and rough sleeping across the EU and the UK.

sources.title: U.S. Dept. of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Annual Homeless Assessment Report (AHAR)
sources.description: Supplies the rigid single-night Point-in-Time (PIT) data for the North American baseline.

sources.title: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC)
sources.description: Offers updated tracking on numbers of conflict and climate-displaced individuals living in temporary encampments, heavily influencing the data for sub-Saharan Africa, Syria, and South American border regions.
